topics.title: The Safe Use of Simple Machines at Home and in the School | Danger of Careless Use of Simple Machines Primary 1 (Basic 1) Term 3 Week 3 Basic Science and Technology
topics.content:
BASIC TECHNOLOGY
BASIC SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
THIRD TERM
WEEK 3
PRIMARY 1
THEME - UNDERSTANDING BASIC TECHNOLOGY
PREVIOUS LESSON - Meaning and Examples of Simple Machines | Importance of Simple Machines Primary 1 (Basic 1) Term 3 Week 2
TOPIC - THE SAFE USE OF SIMPLE MACHINES IN THE HOME
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Safe Use of Simple Machines
3. Dangers of Careless Use of Simple Machines
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives - use simple machines in a safe way in home.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify some of the danger of careless use of some simple machines such as knife, scissor, blade, needles, etc.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of chart showing simple machine used in the home and in the school.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
A simple machine is a device that makes work easy.
For example - broom, spoon, knife, etc.
SAFE USE OF SIMPLE MACHINES AT HOME AND IN THE SCHOOL
The following are safe use of simple machines at home or in the school,
1. Do not play with any simple machine.
2. Dispose properly, if they are broken or not useful anymore.
3. Keep properly after use.
4. Wash after use.
5. Keep properly after use.
6. Handle with care.
7. Turn off electrical simple machines, if not use.
LESSON 2 - DANGERS OF CARELESS USE OF SIMPLE MACHINES
The dangers of careless use of simple machines are as follows:
1. It leads fire outbreak, e.g. match, lighter and all electric appliances.
2. It destroys life and properties, e.g. match, lighter and all electric appliances.
3. It causes bleeding, e.g. knife, cutlass, scissor, needle, etc.
4. It causes temporary or permanent injuries, e.g. all simple machines.
5. It leaves permanent marks or scars, e.g. knife, cutlass, fire, etc.
LESSON 3 - REVISION AND WEEKLY ASSESSMENT (TEST)
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Teacher organizes pupils in groups or pairs depending on the size of the size of the class.
3. Teacher asks pupils to demonstrate the proper use of some simple machines such as knife, broom, spoon, etc.
Pupil’s Activities - Demonstrate the proper use of some simple machines such as knife, broom, spoon, etc.
4. Teacher uses the pupil’s activities in step 3 to introduce the lesson and discuss the Safe use of simple machines.
Pupil’s Activities - Pay attention to the lesson introduction.
5. Teacher demonstrates how to safely use simple machines in home.
Pupil’s Activities - State the safe use of simple machines in the home.
6. Teacher guides pupils to identify the dangers in the use of simple machines in the home.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify dangers in the use of simple machines in the home.
7. Teacher summarizes the lessons on the board with appropriate lesson evaluation.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the summary of the lessons by responding to the questions and writes as instructed.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Meaning and Benefits of Technology | How Things are Done Before and Now Primary 1 (Basic 1) Term 3 Week 4 Basic Science and Technology
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to -
1. mention 3 safe uses of simple machines.
2. mention 3 dangers of careless use of simple machines.

topics.content:
BASIC TECHNOLOGY
BASIC SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY

WEEK 4
PRIMARY 1
THEME - YOU AND TECHNOLOGY
PREVIOUS LESSON - The Safe Use of Simple Machines at Home and in the School | Danger of Careless Use of Simple Machines Primary 1 (Basic 1) Term 3 Week 3 Basic Science and Technology
TOPIC - CONCEPT OF TECHNOLOGY
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Technology
3. Benefits of Technology
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. say what is technology.
2. state the benefits of technology.
3. describe how things are done before and now.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify and differentiate between grinding stone and blender.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of sample or drawing and pictures of technological products.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Technology is the use of knowledge to create new devices or tools.
Technology has made people’s lives and work easier.
For Examples,
1. Television
2. Radio
3. Fan
4. Gas cooker or kerosene stove
5. Fridge
6. Bulbs
7. Padlock, etc.
BENEFITS OF TECHNOLOGY
1. Television, it is used for viewing and listening to programs.
2. Radio, it is used for listening to news and other programs.
3. Fan, it is used for cooling, etc.
4. Motor, it is used for the movement of people and goods from one place to another.
5. Telephone, it is used for making/sending and receiving calls/sms.
6. Gas cooker, it is used for cooking.
LESSON 2 - HOW THINGS ARE DONE BEFORE AND NOW
Teacher organizes pupils in groups or pairs depending on the size of the class to discuss how things are done before and now.
For example - how people move from one place to another, communicate, cook, farm, making fire, preserve food, grind paper, etc.
LESSON 3 - REVISION AND WEEK LESSON ASSESSMENT
As stated in performance objectives or lesson evaluation.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Teacher organizes pupils in groups or pairs depending on the size of the size of the class.
3. Teacher displays sample or chart showing the products of technology.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify and state the benefits of each product of technology.
4. Teacher uses the products of technology to introduce the lesson and leads a discussion on the meaning and benefits of technology.
Pupil’s Activities - Analyze the importance of technology in their communities.
5. Teacher guides pupils to identify and discuss how things are done before and now.
Pupil’s Activities - Discuss how things are done before and now.
6. Teacher summarizes the lessons on the board with appropriate lesson evaluation.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the summary of the lessons by responding to the questions and writes as instructed.
CONCLUSION
- To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
- Next Lesson - Meaning of Electricity and Electric Gadgets | Appliances that Used Electricity | Importance of Electricity Primary 1 (Basic 1) Term 3 Week 5 Basic Science and Technology
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. explain what technology is.
2. mention 5 products of technology.
3. state 5 benefits of technology.
4. describe how people,
- move from one place to another,
- communicate,
- cook,
- farm,
- making fire,
- preserve food,
- grind paper, etc. before technology.

BASIC TECHNOLOGY
BASIC SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
THIRD TERM
WEEK 8
PRIMARY 1
THEME - YOU AND TECHNOLOGY
PREVIOUS LESSON -
TOPIC - CONCEPT OF TECHNOLOGY
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Means of Water Transportation
3. Advantages and Disadvantages of Water Transportation
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. describe water transportation.
2. state different means of water transportation.
3. mention the advantages and disadvantages of water transportation.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify and state different technologies used in water transportation such as boat, ship, etc.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of chart showing technology used in technology.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Transportation is the movement of people and goods from one place to another by land, air and water.
The movement of people and goods from plage to place is known as water transportation.
MEANS OF WATER TRANSPORTATION
Water Transportation is the movement of people and goods from one to another by water.
For example,
1. Ships
2. Boats
3. Ferries
4. Cruise ships
6. Submarines
7. Yacht
LESSON 2 - ADVANTAGES AND DISADVANTAGES OF WATER TRANSPORTATION
ADVANTAGES OF WATER TRANSPORTATION
The advantages of water transportation are as follows:
1. It is less expensive.
2. It is more safer.
3. It has large storage capacity.
4. It is environmental friendly.
DISADVANTAGES OF WATER TRANSPORTATION
The disadvantages of water transportation are as follows:
1. Bad weather
2. Few seaport and ship
3. Poor performance
4. Old equipments
5. Sea weed and ice
6. Lack of maintenance
7. Some of the technology used in water transportation are very expensive.
8. Lack of professional sailor
9. Very slow means of transportation
LESSON 3 - REVISION AND WEEK LESSON ASSESSMENT
As stated in performance objectives or lesson evaluation.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Teacher organizes pupils in groups or pairs depending on the size of the size of the class.
3. Teacher displays different technologies used on water transportation.
4. Teacher lets pupils identify each technology and state their uses.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify each technology and state their uses.
5. Teacher uses the chart and pupil’s responses to introduce the leads a discussion on the meaning and means of water transportation.
Pupil’s Activities - Pay attention to the lesson introduction to explain the meaning of water transportation.
6. Teacher explains the advantages and disadvantages of water transportation.
Pupil’s Activities - Analyze the advantages and disadvantages of water transportation.
7. Teacher summarizes the lessons on the board with appropriate lesson evaluation.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the summary of the lessons by responding to the questions and writes as instructed.
CONCLUSION
- To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
- Next Lesson -
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. explain the meaning of water transportation.
2. state 3 means of water transportation.
3. mention 3 advantages of water transportation.
4. explain 3 disadvantages of water transportation.

topics.content:
BASIC TECHNOLOGY
BASIC SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
THIRD TERM
WEEK 6
PRIMARY 1
THEME - YOU AND TECHNOLOGY
PREVIOUS LESSON - Meaning of Electricity and Electric Gadgets | Appliances that Used Electricity | Importance of Electricity Primary 1 (Basic 1) Term 3 Week 5 Basic Science and Technology
TOPIC - CONCEPT OF TECHNOLOGY
LEARNING AREA
1. Information
2. Meaning of Transportation
3. Means of Land and Air Transportation
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. explain the meaning of transportation.
2. state means of land and air transportation.
2. analyze the importance of land and air transportation.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify and differentiate between the old and modern means of transportations.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of means of land and air transportations.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Transportation is the movement of people and goods from one place to another by land, air and water.
TECHNOLOGY IN TRANSPORTATION
There are many technologies used in transportation,
1. Bicycles
2. Motorcycles
3. Cars
4. Buses
5. Boats
6. Ships
7. Aeroplane
8. Helicopters
9. Trains
10. Animals
MEANS OF TRANSPORTATIONS
There are different means of transportations,
1. Land transportation
2. Air transportation
3. Water transportation
MEANING AND MEANS OF LAND TRANSPORTATION
Land transportation is the movement of people and goods from one place to another by land.
FORMS OF LAND TRANSPORTATION
There are two (2) forms of land transportation.
1. Roads
2. Rail Transportation
TECHNOLOGY IN ROAD TRANSPORTATION
The following are technologies used on road transportation,
1. Bicycles
2. Motorcycles
3. Cars
4. Buses, etc.
LESSON 2 - AIR TRANSPORTATION
Air transportation is the movement of people and goods from one place to another by aeroplane, helicopters, jets, etc.
TECHNOLOGY IN AIR TRANSPORTATION
The following are technologies in Air transportation,
1. Aeroplane
2. Helicopters
3. Space ships
4. Jets, etc.
OLD MEANS OF TRANSPORTATION VERSUS THE NEW ONES
Teacher organizes pupils in groups or pairs depending on the size of the class to discuss and analyzes the means of transportation in the olden days with the modern days.
BENEFITS OF MODERN TRANSPORTATION
The following are the benefits of modern transportation,
1. It is faster.
2. It is safer.
3. It is more comfortable.
4. It is easier.
LESSON 3 - REVISION AND WEEKLY ASSESSMENT (TEST)
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Teacher organizes pupils in groups or pairs depending on the size of the size of the class.
3. Teacher displays chart showing different means of transportation on land and in the air.
4. Teacher asks pupils to identify each mean of transportation and classify them as land and air transportations.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify each mean of transportation and classify them as land and air transportations.
5. Teacher uses the chart and pupil’s responses to introduce the lesson.
Pupil’s Activities - Pay attention to the lesson introduction to understand the concept of the lesson.
6. Teacher leads a discussion on the meaning and means of land and air transportations.
Pupil’s Activities - Differentiate between land and air transportation.
7. Teacher guides pupils to identify and differentiate between old means of transportation. For example, the use of animals and modern technology in transportation.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify and differentiate between old means of transportation.
8. Teacher summarizes the lessons on the board with appropriate lesson evaluation.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the summary of the lessons by responding to the questions and writes as instructed.
CONCLUSION
- To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
- Next Lesson - Technology in Transportation - Meaning and Means of Water Transportation | Advantages and Disadvantages of Water Transportation Primary 1 (Basic 1) Term 3 Week 8 Basic Science and Technology
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. explain the meaning of transportation.
2. mention 5 technologies in transportation.
3. state different types of transportation.
4. differentiate between land and air transportations.
5. mention 3 means of land transportation.
6. state 3 means of air transportation.
7. describe the old and modern means of transportation.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT
1. ________ make lives and work easier.
A. Technology
B. Car
C. Aeroplane
2. ________ is one of the technologies in transportation.
A. Donkey
B. Basket
C. Ship
3. Ship is to ________.
A. Water
B. Land
C. Space
4. Aeroplane is to ________.
A. Water
B. Land
C. Space
5. Train is to ________.
A. Water
B. Land
C. Space

topics.title: Exploring Your Environment - Types and Functions of Roads Primary 1 (Basic 1) Term 3 Week 10 Basic Science and Technology
topics.content:
BASIC SCIENCE
BASIC SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
THIRD TERM
WEEK 10
PRIMARY 3
THEME - LEARNING ABOUT OUR ENVIRONMENT
PREVIOUS LESSON - Exploring Your Environment - Things in and around the Classroom, School and at Home Primary 1 (Basic 1) Term 3 Week 9 Basic Science and Technology
TOPIC - EXPLORING YOUR ENVIRONMENT
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Types of Roads
3. Functions of Roads
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. explain the meaning of road.
2. describe different types of roads.
3. state the importance of roads.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify some of the features of their immediate environment.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Exploring the different types of roads
2. Resourceful person from roads management
3. Other staff must involve in these activities.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Teacher organizes pupils in groups or pairs depending on the size of the class to identify different types of roads within their communities.
For example,
1. Truck C Roads
2. Truck B Roads
3. Truck A Roads
LESSON 2 - MEANING AND TYPES OF ROAD IN NIGERIA
A road is a wide way that link one place another.
Road always links place such streets, communities or states together.
Sometime, road link two or more countries together.
TYPES OF ROAD
1. TRUCK C ROADS
Truck C roads are local or feeder roads constructed, maintained and managed by the Works Department of local government authorities in Nigeria.
For example - Church Street to Baal Street.
2. TRUCK B ROADS
Truck B roads are the state roads that links major cities within the state.
For example - Mile 2 to Oshodi
These roads are constructed, maintained and managed by the state government.
3. TRUCK A ROADS
Truck C roads are the federal roads that links major states within the country such as Nigeria.
For example - Lagos to Ibadan Expressways
These roads are constructed, maintained and managed by the federal government.
Note - Give examples of each roads based on the pupil’s localities.
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF ROAD
The importance of road are as follows:
1. It links the streets, communities and states together.
2. It is less expensive compared with other means of transportation.
3. It is flexible and easy to manage.
4. It promotes unity among people of different cultures.
5. It leads to growth and development.
6. It is suitable for short distance.
7. It provides door to door services.
8. It brings goods and services to the people.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Teacher organizes pupils in groups or pairs depending on the size of the class.
3. Teacher takes pupils out for a walk with the community to identify different types of roads within around them.
4. Teacher asks pupils to identify and differentiate between these roads.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify and differentiate between these roads.
5. Teacher uses the trip and pupil’s responses to introduce the lesson and leads a discussion on the meaning and types of roads.
Pupil’s Activities - Explain the meaning and types of roads.
6. Teacher explains the importance of roads.
Pupil’s Activities - Analyze the importance of roads in their communities.
7. Teacher summarizes the lessons on the board with appropriate lesson evaluation.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the summary of the lesson by responding correctly to the questions and write as instructed.
CONCLUSION
- To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
- Next Lesson - Exploring Your Environment - Things in and around the Classroom, School and at Home (Primary 1)
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. explain the meaning of road.
2. state 3 major types of roads in your community.
3, differentiate between truck A, B, and C types of roads.
4. give 3 examples of local roads in their communities.
5. mention 3 examples of state roads.
6. state 3 examples of federal roads.
7. analyze 4 importance of roads your community.
